articles.headline: Coles Group Investigates Cyber Incident, No Data Loss Confirmed
articles.summary: Australian supermarket giant Coles Group has announced it is investigating a cybersecurity incident. In a statement to the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) on November 16, 2026, the company confirmed its retail and online operations remain unaffected. Crucially, Coles stated that its investigation has so far found no evidence that customer, employee, or supplier data has been compromised or exfiltrated. The company is working with the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC).

articles.headline: Google Project Zero Ends 30-Day Grace Period for Disclosures
articles.summary: Google's Project Zero, an elite vulnerability research team, has announced a significant change to its disclosure policy. Effective immediately, the team is eliminating the 30-day grace period previously granted for patch adoption. Under the new "Full X" policy, technical details of a vulnerability will be made public 90 days after reporting to a vendor, regardless of whether a fix is available. The deadline will be progressively shortened to 30 days by 2028 to pressure vendors into faster patching cycles.

articles.headline: Kroll Report: 69% of Organizations Breached in Past Year
articles.summary: Kroll's 2026 Data Breach Outlook report reveals a troubling landscape, with 69% of global organizations experiencing a data breach in the past year and 34% suffering more than one. The financial services industry was the most affected sector, accounting for 20% of breaches handled by Kroll. A key finding highlights the immense impact of supply chain risk, with 69% of all affected individuals being impacted by a breach at a third-party provider, often in the technology sector.

articles.headline: Qatar Partners with SignQuantum for Post-Quantum Cybersecurity
articles.summary: The government of Qatar is taking proactive steps to prepare for the threat of quantum computing by partnering with the cybersecurity firm SignQuantum. The collaboration, led by Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT), will focus on exploring applications for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and developing quantum-resistant digital signatures to secure government services and data against future threats.

articles.headline: 'n0n' Extortion Group Claims Breach of Visa, Mastercard, JPMorgan
articles.summary: The data extortion group 'n0n' has made an unverified claim of stealing a trove of customer and marketing data from financial giants Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase. The group, which operates by stealing data and threatening to leak it without deploying ransomware, has not provided proof. The allegedly stolen data includes cardholder profiles and booking information. None of the named companies have confirmed a breach.

articles.headline: BYOD Ransomware Group Claims Breach of Michigan State University
articles.summary: The 'BYOD' ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a major data breach at Michigan State University (MSU), alleging the exfiltration of 1.03 million records containing personal identifiable information (PII) and passwords for current and former students and staff. The group publicly stated that the university's incident response team failed to maintain communication after an initial contact, leading the attackers to leak the data.

articles.headline: German Drone Maker Quantum Systems Hit by Cyberattack
articles.summary: German defense and aerospace company Quantum Systems, a manufacturer of drones, confirmed it was the target of a cyberattack in late October 2026. While the company states the attack was contained and poses no risk to customers, reports suggest the incident may have involved a malicious software update, raising serious supply chain security concerns. German federal authorities, including military counterintelligence, are investigating the attack.

articles.headline: Critical UnrealIRCd Flaw (CVE-2026-114713) Actively Exploited
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in the UnrealIRCd server, tracked as CVE-2026-114713 with a CVSS score of 8.6, is being actively exploited in the wild just one day after a patch was released. The flaw allows for command execution with server privileges. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to apply the patch by November 16, 2026.

publications.headline: UnrealIRCd Flaw, AI Supply Chain Attack, and PostgreSQL RCE Highlight Cybersecurity Risks

articles.headline: Hacker Group Claims Breach of Brazilian University, Affecting 53,000
articles.summary: The threat actor group BLCKORDER has claimed responsibility for a data breach at Celso Lisboa University in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. A user on a dark web forum is advertising a database for sale, allegedly containing the records of 51,000 students and 2,000 employees. The claim, while unverified, highlights the continued targeting of the education sector by cybercriminals seeking to steal large volumes of personal data.

articles.headline: Momentum Telecom Breach Claim Alleges 7.5M User Records for Sale
articles.summary: A threat actor, 'Torax2020,' has posted an unverified claim on a criminal forum alleging a data breach at Momentum Telecom, a provider of cloud voice services. The actor is offering for sale two data files said to contain the personally identifiable information (PII) of over 7.5 million users. The data was allegedly exfiltrated earlier in 2026. While the claim has not been confirmed by the company, it highlights the ongoing trend of large-scale data breaches targeting telecommunications providers.

articles.headline: Taiwan Funeral Operator Hacked Fire Dept to Illegally Solicit Clients
articles.summary: A funeral service operator in Taiwan has been arrested for allegedly hiring hackers to breach the emergency dispatch systems of the Taoyuan Fire Department and National Fire Agency. The group stole personal data from emergency records, allowing the operator to illegally solicit business from the families of deceased individuals by falsely claiming to be government-assigned. The case highlights a unique and predatory motive for cybercrime, leading to three arrests for violations of cybersecurity and data protection laws.

articles.headline: ConnectWise Probes ScreenConnect Partner Account Compromise
articles.summary: ConnectWise is actively investigating reports of unauthorized access to its partners' ScreenConnect accounts. The incident is being treated as a supply chain attack, as threat actors have successfully used their access to deploy unauthorized remote-access software into the environments of downstream customers. The compromise of a powerful RMM tool like ScreenConnect represents a significant threat, potentially giving attackers administrative access to a multitude of client networks.

articles.headline: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old RCE Bug
articles.summary: The PostgreSQL project has issued a significant minor version update that remediates 52 vulnerabilities. Most notably, the patch addresses a critical, 22-year-old remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability. Although the flaw requires authentication to exploit, it poses a substantial risk in many environments where credentials may be compromised. The discovery highlights the persistent danger of legacy bugs in mature, widely-trusted open-source projects and reinforces the need for diligent patch management.

articles.headline: Stolen AI Key at Fireworks AI Triggers Supply Chain Attack on Cursor
articles.summary: A sophisticated supply chain attack began with a stolen API key from AI provider Fireworks AI, allowing attackers to breach developer tool company Cursor. The threat actors then injected a trojanized version of the popular 'Claude Code' VS Code extension into Cursor's marketplace. For 11 hours, approximately 5,000 developers downloaded the malicious extension, which installed a persistent SSH backdoor on their systems, highlighting the cascading risks in AI-powered development workflows.

articles.headline: Check Point Zero-Day Exploited to Deploy Destructive ESXi Wipers
articles.summary: A critical zero-day vulnerability in Check Point's Gaia OS, CVE-2026-123039, is being actively exploited in the wild. Attackers are chaining an initial access vulnerability with this local privilege escalation flaw to gain root on security gateways. Once compromised, the gateways are used as a pivot point to deploy destructive wiper malware on VMware ESXi servers, impacting dozens of organizations and prompting CISA to add the flaw to its KEV catalog.

articles.headline: UnrealIRCd Command Injection Flaw Added to CISA KEV Catalog
articles.summary: The U.S. CISA has added a critical command injection vulnerability in the UnrealIRCd server, CVE-2026-114713, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The flaw, which stems from improper neutralization of delimiters, is confirmed to be under active exploitation. It allows attackers to inject and execute commands on vulnerable servers, posing a significant risk to organizations using the popular open-source IRC daemon. Federal agencies are now mandated to patch the vulnerability.
